desc: The precedence partial order: takes-precedence semantics, rank modifications, incidental admission, reconsider's split rank, the appeal-yield matrix, and the per-motion applicability table. Conditions are expressions per INTERFACE.md; bindings: m = motion id being moved, t = target frame or null.

semantics.takes_precedence_over: takes-precedence-over(B, A) iff B may be moved and stated while A is pending, whereupon B becomes the immediately pending question [5:8]
semantics.unwind: pending motions are voted in reverse order of stating (LIFO), stopping if any of the halting motions named in [10:34] carries: recess, lay-on-table, postpone-to-certain-time, commit, or postpone-indefinitely (adjourn, when adopted, likewise ends consideration, but via session/meeting end [21:7] rather than the 10:34 list — engine.json unwind is authoritative)
semantics.ranked_chain: the ranked chain (registry.json, rank 1-13) is a total order [5:11]; incidental motions have no rank among themselves [5:12, 6:19]

rank_modifications.rule: amend applied to any amendable motion takes precedence over its target, even a target above rank 3; effective_rank is positional: rank(amend applied to F) = just-above(rank(F)); secondary amendment sits just above the primary it amends; no third degree
degrees-of-amendment cap: at most one primary and one secondary amendment pending per amended target at a time (relaxed by the filling-blanks device, registry data outside the stack cap)

limit-extend-debate applies to any immediately pending debatable motion or a consecutive series from it; previous-question likewise to any immediately pending debatable-or-amendable motion or series; both thereby out-rank their targets in the moment of application
subsidiary motions cannot be applied to one another except per each SDC-2 (e.g., nothing tables an amendment alone — the main question goes with it)

incidental_admission.rule: an incidental motion is in order only while legitimately-incidental (guard) to a pending motion or to business at hand; it then takes precedence over the question(s) it arises from and must be decided first [6:18]. It yields to motions of higher rank than the question it arose from, not to lower ones [6:21], and generally yields to privileged motions and (if adhering) to lay-on-table [6:19, 23:2(1)].
incidental_admission.yield_expr_note: compiled into the push test: an incidental frame I with origin frame O admits a new motion N iff [">", ["erank-of-motion", N], ["erank", O]] or N is privileged or (N = lay-on-table and I adheres) — overridden by table/appeal-yield-matrix for appeals/submitted points, and void for division-of-assembly

overrides.rule: division-of-assembly is excepted from the general yield rule entirely — it yields to nothing under this rule

pending appeals / submitted points of order follow table/appeal-yield-matrix, not the generic rule — in particular, an undebatable adhering appeal admits no subsidiary except lay-on-table via the main question, even one out-ranking its origin
every motion yields to motions legitimately incidental to itself; where a per-motion SDC-2 condition conflicts with the generic rule, the per-motion condition wins

reconsider_split_rank.making: outranks everything, including rank 13 and a pending vote-to-adjourn before declaration [37:9(1a), 21:10]; recorded and held (engine.json reconsider_held — suspends execution of the reconsidered vote [37:11]) without pushing a frame
reconsider_split_rank.consideration: carries only the target's rank [37:9(1b)]: taken up immediately if the target would then be in order, else queued into the pending series at the target's rank position and taken up when all higher frames are disposed of [37:25-27]
reconsider_split_rank.enter_minutes: reconsider-enter-minutes outranks plain reconsider at making time and cannot be called up the day made (exceptions per registry record) [37:47(2), 37:46-47]

table/appeal-yield-matrix.desc: The general incidental rule is wrong for appeals unless refined by this four-case table [24:3(1)-(2)], mirrored for points of order the chair submits to the assembly [23:2(1)-(2)]. Case selection: debatable = ["debatable", appeal-frame]; adhering = ["!=", ["adheres-to", appeal-frame], null].

cases.note: commit/postpone/table reach it only applied to the main question, carrying the appeal along
yields to NO other subsidiary — even one out-ranking the motion it arose from
yields to no subsidiary at all

table/applicability.desc: Per-motion admissibility beyond the bare rank test (which is engine.json push_legality). applies_to: predicate over the target frame t (null target = the motion relates to no pending question). out_of_order_when: disjuncts — the motion is out of order if ANY expr is true; each carries its citation, so a blocked action's justification is the true disjunct and an allowed action's justification is the falsity of all. Chart I's right-hand column [t4-t5] is the source checklist for the ranked rows.

table/applicability.generic_incidental_note: Incidental motions without a row here (suspend-rules, division-of-question, consideration-by-paragraph, voting/nomination motions, requests) admit via guard/legitimately-incidental plus their registry-record conditions (windows, timeliness); their yield behavior is incidental_admission plus table/appeal-yield-matrix where applicable.
